response.text:
Recent work supports separating contradiction from missing evidence. ACL 2025’s [CAQA benchmark](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.837.pdf) distinguishes supportive, partially supportive, contradictory and irrelevant evidence. Applied to this task, a proposed audit taxonomy is: redundancy, explicit device incompatibility, and insufficient evidence for current intent. Attach item IDs and exact title/description spans to each finding. Repeated attributes establish similarity; they do not establish unwanted repetition. Mark incompatibility only when an explicit requirement conflicts with documented product support. Missing device, occasion or intent information should yield “unknown,” never an inferred mismatch. These are task-specific adaptations, not a validated recommendation taxonomy.

Abstention requires validation: [AbstentionBench (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09038) finds persistent failures on underspecified questions, with prompting helpful but insufficient. Human review also needs controls: [Human Feedback Is Not Gold Standard (2024)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/f719b8ca81221f380836e573d479c223-Abstract-Conference.html) identifies confounding in preference and error judgments; [annotation-assistance research (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06778) finds automated annotation less reliable than experts. Practical synthesis: independently double-annotate a small, category-balanced calibration set containing clear contradictions, supported matches and ambiguous cases; adjudicate disagreements and report per-label precision, agreement and abstention coverage. Preserve unavailable attributes as unknown, never equate later nonpurchase with rejection, and use findings as diagnostic evidence without adding a separately fitted scoring model.
